tools.name: list_my_products
tools.description: Use once per repository, before the other 6to9 tools, when you do not yet know which 6to9 product this codebase is (there is no .6to9.json at the repo root). Lists the products on the user's 6to9 account with their site urls and audience segments. Match the repo's own site url against each product's url to SUGGEST one, confirm with the user once, then save {"product_id": "<id>"} as .6to9.json and pass it as `product` from then on. Each product lists its audiences (ICPs) with who buys, their trigger, the pitch and research_state — use these to infer which audience the current task serves.

tools.name: recommend_features
tools.description: Use when the user is working on, or asking what to do about, a product surface or growth problem: the landing page or hero, signup or login, onboarding, the pricing page, core app flows, what to build next, low conversion / activation / signups, or how competitors do something. Call it BEFORE designing or building such a change, even if nobody mentions 6to9. Returns 6to9's ranked recommendations for this product from its competitor research: 3-5 items, each with why it fits this product (which rivals ship it, the evidence, the audience segment, whether it is already built or planned), plus a lead pick with a build-spec summary. Items the founder already chose or put in Build rank first. With no segment, the answer also carries groups: the top picks for each audience. Next, call get_build_spec on the item you will build. If the area has not been researched it says so and lists the nearest research: relay that honestly.

product.description: The 6to9 product id for this repository: the product_id in .6to9.json at the repo root, or an id from list_my_products. Omit it when the account has one product.
product.title: Product

area.description: The part of the product, in plain words: 'landing hero', 'signup', 'onboarding', 'pricing page', 'core flows'. Omit for the whole product.
area.title: Area

segment.description: An audience (ICP) slug from list_my_products or the segment in .6to9.json. Omit it to get recommendations grouped by audience.
segment.title: Segment

query.description: Optional free text matched against item titles and reasons.
query.title: Query

goal.description: Optional. One or two sentences on the problem in the user's own terms, with AGGREGATE context only, e.g. 'landing gets ~2k visits a week but ~1% sign up'. Never user-level data, secrets or code. Used only to order and explain the picks.
goal.title: Goal

tools.name: get_build_spec
tools.description: Use when you are about to build one of 6to9's recommended features, or the user asks for a build-ready spec or prompt for it. Returns the composed build prompt (exactly what the founder gets from 'Copy prompt' in the 6to9 portal, bound to the artifact they picked) plus its competitor evidence and visuals. Build from the prompt and keep the artifact it binds in view; cite only the evidence it contains. build_options lists the spec's artifacts, ranked best first — open one with get_artifact (pass building=true when building: only then does it return the source), record the founder's choice with pick_artifact, and don't build from one marked OUTDATED (STYLE OUTDATED is look-only — its content is current; the option says what to do). Address the item by spec_id (from recommend_features), or by segment + surface + slug (+ rival for remix items). Pass building=true only when you are actually going to build it: that registers it in the team's Build tracker.

product.description: The 6to9 product id for this repository: the product_id in .6to9.json at the repo root, or an id from list_my_products. Omit it when the account has one product.

spec_id.description: The item's spec_id from recommend_features: the direct path.

tools.name: start_research
tools.description: Use when recommend_features or get_build_spec say an area, audience or item is not researched, or the user asks 6to9 to research something — a new audience, one specific feature, or 'dig deeper into X' via focus. Call it only after the user asked for the research or said yes to your offer — it starts it (several minutes, in the background). Only when 6to9 returns a quote (e.g. credits are needed) must you show it and ask before calling again with confirm=<token> from THAT quote. It can also come back already queued/running (with a run_id for get_research_status), already researched, on a cooldown, or over today's cap — relay whichever it says. Render every field 6to9 sends back, including ones you don't recognise: if it points at a link or a cost, send the user there and do not retry. To change an existing spec's text, use refine_spec — it researches first by itself if it needs to.

product.description: The 6to9 product id for this repository: the product_id in .6to9.json at the repo root, or an id from list_my_products. Omit it when the account has one product.

confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: get_research_status

tools.name: refine_spec
tools.description: Use when the user wants to change an existing 6to9 feature spec's TEXT — 'too generic', 'make it mobile-first', 'shorter copy', 'target teams'. 6to9 revises only what the instruction needs, keeps the rest, and saves the old version (revert_spec undoes it). Use the user's own words as the instruction. Not for an artifact's look (demo, mock, rival component) — use refine_artifact for that, with feedback on the one artifact to change. If the change needs research 6to9 does not have yet, this starts it and returns a run_id; if the spec itself is an unresearched idea, it changes nothing and says to research it. Call only for a change the user asked for; each call counts toward 6to9's daily limits. Never include user-level data, secrets or code.

spec_id.title: Spec Id

instruction.description: What to change, in the user's own words. Trimmed to 500 chars.
instruction.title: Instruction

Not for the spec's text — use refine_spec for that. Call only for a change the user asked for; each call counts toward 6to9's daily limits. Never include user-level data, secrets or code.

tools.name: show_idea
tools.description: Use when the user wants to SEE a feature idea or spec from 6to9 that has nothing to show yet, or asks for new visuals of it — 'show me this idea', 'what would it look like', 'is there a demo'. It MAKES new visuals and costs a run: to show what an idea already has, call view_idea instead (free), and use this only when view_idea finds nothing. The same as the portal's 'Show me this idea' button: in one run 6to9 builds a working demo, a mock in the user's own product's style, and rival variants (how competitors ship it), keeping whichever of the three it could make. Takes a couple of minutes. It is paid work that counts toward 6to9's daily limits: call it only when the user asked to see it or said yes to your offer, and only once per ask. Afterwards, list_artifacts (or get_build_spec) shows what landed.

tools.name: add_audience
tools.description: Use when the user asks 6to9 to research, or to track, an audience (ICP) that is not among the product's audiences in list_my_products — only on their ask, never on your own initiative. 6to9 first checks it against every audience it already has: if it is the same audience under another name, nothing is added and you are told which one it matches — offer that one instead. A new audience is live in the founder's 6to9 portal immediately and takes one of the product's 8 active audience slots — tell the user so; to undo it, they archive it in the portal. Its slug is returned; it is NOT researched until you call start_research(audience=<slug>), which you do only if the user wants it researched.

tools.name: list_artifacts
tools.description: Use to see what a 6to9 feature spec can be built from, or before changing, picking or opening one of its visuals. A spec is its text plus ARTIFACTS, ranked best first: a working demo (live HTML), the generated mock (an image), rival components (captures of what rivals ship — evidence, never edited), restyles, and our own versions derived from a rival. Each has an artifact_id, whether it is the founder's pick, and whether it is OUTDATED (made from older spec text — don't build from it until 6to9 has refreshed it) or STYLE OUTDATED (a demo built with an earlier version of the founder's site style — its content is current). One marked 'chosen on purpose' is an earlier version the founder went back to — build from it; 6to9 leaves it as it is. Free and read-only; opening an OUTDATED one with get_artifact starts its refresh (paid, once per change).

tools.name: get_artifact
tools.description: Use to open one artifact from list_artifacts or get_build_spec's build_options. Pass building=true when building it into this repo: only then does it return the HTML source to port — an HTML artifact (a working demo, or our own version of a rival component) returns its full source, an image its URL. Otherwise the artifact is shown to the user (an interactive idea card where the chat supports it, else a preview image and the live link) and no source is returned. If it is outdated, 6to9 starts refreshing it and says so — tell the user and check back rather than building from it. One marked 'chosen on purpose' is an earlier version the founder went back to — build from it (no refresh starts). Free, except that opening an OUTDATED artifact starts its refresh (paid, once per change).

tools.name: refine_artifact
tools.description: Use when the user wants one of a spec's artifacts changed — 'make the demo show only 3 slots', 'darker mock', 'make our own version of Calendly's picker'. Pass the user's own words. 6to9 decides whether the feedback only changes this artifact's look or changes the feature itself — then it also updates the spec text and the other artifacts follow it, so don't also call refine_spec. Refining a rival capture makes our own version and leaves the capture as it is. Paid: only on the user's ask, once per ask; it can take a few minutes. Never include user-level data, secrets or code.
